questions.enonce_markdown:
The following diagram shows the relationship between the molecular formula of some compounds

![fig-1](gce-al-chemistry-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

In the diagram, W ($\mathrm{C_3H_8O}$) reacts with Na to give Y + $\mathrm{H_2}$, with $\mathrm{P/I_2}$ to give Z, with $\mathrm{I_2/OH^-}$ to give $\mathrm{CHI_3}$, and is converted to X ($\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$).

(i) Give the name and write the structural formulae for the isomers of W.

(ii) Which of these isomers in a(i) correspond to the compound W?

Give a reason

(iii) Identify the compounds X, Y and Z

X.

Y.

Z.

(iv) Give the reagent and conditions for the conversion of W to X

(v) Give the name and colour of $\mathrm{CHI_3}$. *[10 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Three structural isomers have the formula $\mathrm{C_3H_8O}$:

- **propan-1-ol**, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2OH}$;
- **propan-2-ol**, $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3}$;
- **methoxyethane** (ethyl methyl ether), $\mathrm{CH_3OCH_2CH_3}$.

**(ii)** W is **propan-2-ol**, $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3}$. Reasons: W reacts with sodium to give hydrogen, so it has an -OH group (this rules out the ether); it gives the **iodoform reaction** (triiodomethane with $\mathrm{I_2/OH^-}$), which requires the group $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)-}$; only propan-2-ol has it (propan-1-ol has $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2-}$ and does not). Its oxidation also gives a ketone, $\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$.

**(iii)**

- **X = propanone**, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$, formed by oxidation of the secondary alcohol.
- **Y = sodium propan-2-oxide** (sodium isopropoxide), $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHONa}$: $2\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHOH} + 2\mathrm{Na} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHONa} + \mathrm{H_2}$
- **Z = 2-iodopropane**, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHI}$, formed by $\mathrm{P/I_2}$ (phosphorus(III) iodide made in situ): $3\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHOH} + \mathrm{PI_3} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHI} + \mathrm{H_3PO_3}$

**(iv)** W to X: **acidified potassium dichromate(VI)** ($\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ / dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$) **heated** (warm, under reflux); the orange solution turns green. $3\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHOH} + \mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}} + 8\mathrm{H^{+}} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CO} + 2\mathrm{Cr^{3+}} + 7\mathrm{H_2O}$ (Acidified potassium manganate(VII) also works.)

**(v)** $\mathrm{CHI_3}$ is **triiodomethane (iodoform)**, a **pale yellow** solid with an antiseptic smell: $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3} + 4\mathrm{I_2} + 6\mathrm{OH^{-}} \rightarrow \mathrm{CHI_3} + \mathrm{CH_3COO^{-}} + 5\mathrm{I^{-}} + 5\mathrm{H_2O}$

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is hybridization?

(ii) Give one example of an sp hybridized molecule. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Hybridisation is the **mixing (combination) of atomic orbitals of similar energy on the same atom to form the same number of new, equivalent hybrid orbitals** of intermediate energy and definite directions in space (e.g. one s and one p orbital give two sp orbitals; one s and three p give four $sp^3$ orbitals). The hybrid orbitals then overlap with orbitals of other atoms to form sigma bonds.

**(ii)** **Ethyne**, $\mathrm{C_2H_2}$ ($\mathrm{H-C\equiv C-H}$): each carbon uses two sp hybrid orbitals for its two sigma bonds (linear, $180^\circ$), the two unhybridised p orbitals forming the two pi bonds. Other examples: $\mathrm{BeCl_2}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Suggest a chemical test which could be used to distinguish between the following pairs of compounds.

(i) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_2CH_2}$

(ii) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$ *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Ethane and ethene:** shake each gas with **bromine water** (or bromine in an inert solvent). Ethene **decolourises** the orange-brown bromine water quickly, by addition across the double bond: $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{Br_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_2BrCH_2Br}$. Ethane, a saturated alkane, gives **no change** in the dark. (Alternative: ethene decolourises acidified potassium manganate(VII); ethane does not.)

**(ii) Propanal and propanone:** warm each with **Tollens' reagent** (ammoniacal silver nitrate, $[\mathrm{Ag(NH_3)_2}]^+$). The aldehyde propanal is oxidised and gives a **silver mirror**; the ketone propanone gives **no reaction**: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO} + 2\mathrm{[Ag(NH_3)_2]^{+}} + 3\mathrm{OH^{-}} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2COO^{-}} + 2\mathrm{Ag} + 4\mathrm{NH_3} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$ (Alternative: with warm Fehling's solution propanal gives a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide; propanone gives none.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
State the reagent and reaction conditions for the following conversion

![fig-2](gce-al-chemistry-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_2.png)

(phenylamine, $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$, to benzenediazonium chloride, $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-}$) *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reagent:** **sodium nitrite solution (NaNO$_2$) and dilute hydrochloric acid** (these generate nitrous acid, $\mathrm{HNO_2}$, in situ). **Conditions:** the mixture must be kept **cold, between 0 and 5 $^\circ$C** (ice bath), because above about 10 $^\circ$C the diazonium salt decomposes to phenol and nitrogen gas.

$\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2} + \mathrm{NaNO_2} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^{+}} + \mathrm{Cl^{-}} + \mathrm{NaCl} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$
